name: test-tier-definitions
body:
The repo defines exactly three test tiers, durably, and a test's tier is decided by what it exercises, not by where it lives or how it is named. `unit` tests exactly one unit (one function/struct/component) with everything else faked. `integration` tests two or more units together with everything else faked. `e2e` tests one or more units with real I/O. Unit and integration share one strict purity rule — no real I/O — pinned as `global.constraint.test-tier-boundaries` and decomposed in the children below; e2e is the only tier allowed real I/O.

Tier assignment is decidable from the test itself: a test that opens a file, a database, a git repo, or spawns a process is NOT a unit or integration test, whatever it is called — it is e2e by definition (requirements.requirement.no-real-io-boundary).

AC (review-checked prose law): the three definitions and the boundary are stated in the global constraint; a new test can be classified into exactly one tier from its I/O and its unit count alone.
